title: Export variety and imported intermediate inputs: industry-level evidence from Africa
summary: Using manufacturing industry-level data for 26 African countries, the paper finds strong evidence of a positive relationship between imported intermediate inputs and the variety of exported products. Imported inputs help because they are lower-priced and embody higher quality and technology.
keyFindings: Imported intermediate inputs are positively related to the variety of products a country exports.
The effect works through lower prices and higher-quality, technology-embodied inputs.
The effect depends on an industry's absorptive capacity, especially when inputs come from advanced countries.
methods: Manufacturing industry-level panel data across 26 African countries, 1995–2016.
